newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE SHARES END LOWER, ELECTRICITY SECTOR SLIDES.
newsitem.headline: CHILE SHARES END LOWER, ELECTRICITY SECTOR SLIDES.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed sharply lower in thin trade with the market dragged down by tumbles in the heavyweight electricity industry, said traders.
The bolsa is seen resuming its downward tilt at the opening as jitters mount ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's talks August 19, they said.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended down 1.28 percent at 132.37 points. The general .IGPA index lost 0.71 percent to 5,642.37 points.
Turnover plunged to just seven billion pesos from 20.6 billion pesos on Friday.
The sharpest falls included the Enersis energy group, which tumbled on concerns about the impact of the deal with Endesa Espana on the company's future polices, said dealers.
"There will be important changes in the management and investment policies. But it's not clear what will happen and this is causing a scare," said one dealer.
Enersis dropped 1.15 percent to 300-1/2 pesos, while subsidiary Endesa fell 2.49 percent to 313-1/2 pesos.
The two companies account for around a 30 percent weighting in the IPSA index.
Other traders said the low turnover reflected the fact that investors were still analyzing company second quarter results that were published at the end of last month.
Winners included bottler Andina, up 1.02 percent at 1,480 pesos and Banco Edwards, which rose 0.48 percent to 52-3/4 pesos.
